tile_summary: Vegetable carbon is an intensely black colouring made from carbon-rich plant material.
expanded_summary: Vegetable carbon is an intensely black colouring made from carbon-rich plant material. The material is carbonised and purified rather than used as ordinary charcoal.
source_preparation_copy: Produced by controlled carbonisation of vegetable material followed by purification and fine processing.
fact_1_copy: Used for black or very dark colouring.
fact_2_copy: The carbon can originate from plant material even though the final ingredient is predominantly elemental carbon.
evidence_copy: Europe's earlier assessment found no safety concern at reported uses provided residues of potentially cancer-causing combustion chemicals were tightly limited. In 2026, the authority confirmed that commercial 153 can contain many very small particles, including nanoparticles, but said the submitted particle information was not sufficient to complete a nanoscale assessment. This is a defined gap about particle behaviour and specifications; it is not evidence that eating 153 has been shown to cause harm.

tile_summary: Sodium sulphite is a sulphite salt used to preserve foods and control browning.
expanded_summary: Sodium sulphite is a sulphite salt used to preserve foods and control browning. In food it can release sulphur dioxide-related preserving species.
source_preparation_copy: Manufactured by reacting sulphur dioxide with a sodium alkali and crystallising the salt.
fact_1_copy: Part of the sulphite preservative family.
fact_2_copy: Used for preservation, antioxidant action and browning control.

tile_summary: Potassium sulphite is a salt in the sulphite family, used for preservation and antioxidant effects.
expanded_summary: Potassium sulphite is a potassium salt in the sulphite preservative family, chemically related to sulphur dioxide and other sulphites. It is used for preservation and as an antioxidant.
source_preparation_copy: Manufactured by neutralising sulphur dioxide with a potassium alkali.
fact_1_copy: Used for preservation and antioxidant effects.
fact_2_copy: Chemically related to sulphur dioxide and other sulphites.

tile_summary: Gamma-tocopherol is one of the naturally occurring tocopherols in the vitamin E family.
expanded_summary: Gamma-tocopherol is one of the naturally occurring tocopherols in the vitamin E family. It is fat-soluble and can help slow oxidation.
source_preparation_copy: Commercial food-grade material is commonly isolated and purified from vegetable-oil fractions rich in tocopherols.
fact_1_copy: Found naturally in vegetable oils and other plant foods.
fact_2_copy: Used as an antioxidant in fat-containing foods.

tile_summary: Potassium adipate is a potassium salt of adipic acid, a manufactured acid.
expanded_summary: Potassium adipate is a potassium salt of adipic acid, a manufactured acid with two acid groups (a dicarboxylic acid). It is used mainly for acidity control or related processing functions.
source_preparation_copy: Made by neutralising adipic acid with a potassium-containing base and purifying the salt.
fact_2_copy: Used mainly for acidity control or related processing functions.

tile_summary: Ferric ammonium citrate is an iron-containing citrate complex rather than a single simple salt.
expanded_summary: Ferric ammonium citrate is an iron-containing citrate complex rather than a single simple salt. It combines iron with citrate and ammonium in a water-compatible form.
source_preparation_copy: Prepared by reacting iron compounds, citric acid and ammonia under controlled conditions and drying the resulting complex.
fact_1_copy: A complex of iron with citrate and ammonium, not simply iron metal or plain citric acid.
fact_2_copy: Used where iron and citrate chemistry provides the desired technological effect.

tile_summary: Polysorbate 20 is an emulsifier made from sorbitol-derived material, polyoxyethylene chains and lauric acid.
expanded_summary: Polysorbate 20 is an emulsifier made from sorbitol-derived material, polyoxyethylene chains and lauric acid. Its molecular design gives it both water-friendly and fat-friendly parts.
source_preparation_copy: Produced by esterifying sorbitol/sorbitan with fatty acids and adding polyoxyethylene chains through controlled chemical processing.
fact_1_copy: Helps oils, fats and water stay mixed and can stabilise foams or dispersions.
fact_2_copy: The fatty-acid feedstock may come from plant or animal fats, while the final emulsifier is chemically processed.

entry_title: Diacetyltartaric and fatty acid esters of glycerol (472e)
consumer_display_name: Diacetyltartaric and fatty acid esters of glycerol
tile_summary: Diacetyltartaric and fatty acid esters of glycerol are emulsifiers made by adding diacetyltartaric acid-derived groups to mono- and diglyceride-type fat molecules.
expanded_summary: Diacetyltartaric and fatty acid esters of glycerol are emulsifiers made by adding diacetyltartaric acid-derived groups to mono- and diglyceride-type fat molecules. The modification changes how the molecules interact with dough, fat and water.
source_preparation_copy: Made from glycerol/fatty-acid materials plus diacetyltartaric acid-derived components through controlled esterification; fatty-acid sources can be plant or animal.
fact_1_copy: Built on glycerol and fatty acids, the same broad building blocks found in edible fats.
fact_2_copy: Used as emulsifiers and texture/process aids, with some forms particularly important in bakery applications.

tile_summary: Disodium 5′-guanylate is the disodium salt of a guanosine nucleotide.
expanded_summary: Disodium 5′-guanylate is the disodium salt of a guanosine nucleotide. These nucleotide flavour enhancers strongly boost savoury taste, especially when used together with glutamate.
source_preparation_copy: Commercial food-grade nucleotide salts are commonly produced from microbial fermentation or enzymatic processing of biological nucleotide material, then purified and converted to the sodium salt.
fact_1_copy: Guanylate and inosinate can amplify umami far more strongly when combined with glutamate than when used alone.
fact_2_copy: Related nucleotide compounds occur naturally in foods and cells.
fact_3_copy: Used as flavour enhancers in savoury foods.

tile_summary: Disodium 5′-inosinate is the disodium salt of an inosine nucleotide that boosts savoury umami taste.
expanded_summary: Disodium 5′-inosinate is the disodium salt of an inosine nucleotide. Nucleotide flavour enhancers strongly boost savoury taste, especially when used with glutamate.
source_preparation_copy: Commercial food-grade nucleotide salts are commonly produced from microbial fermentation or enzymatic processing of biological nucleotide material, then purified and converted to the sodium salt.
fact_1_copy: Guanylate and inosinate can amplify umami far more strongly when combined with glutamate than when used alone.
fact_2_copy: Related nucleotide compounds occur naturally in foods and cells.
fact_3_copy: Used as flavour enhancers in savoury foods.

tile_summary: L-cysteine hydrochloride is a salt of L-cysteine, a sulphur-containing amino acid found naturally in proteins.
expanded_summary: L-cysteine hydrochloride is a salt of L-cysteine, a sulphur-containing amino acid found naturally in proteins. In food processing it is particularly known for changing dough properties.
source_preparation_copy: Modern food-grade L-cysteine can be produced by microbial fermentation or other controlled manufacturing routes, then converted to the hydrochloride salt and purified.
fact_1_copy: Cysteine is a normal amino-acid component of many proteins.
fact_2_copy: Can act as a flour treatment agent by modifying disulphide bonds in dough proteins.
fact_3_copy: The additive number does not by itself disclose the manufacturing source, so source-specific dietary concerns require product or supplier information.

tile_summary: Isobutane is a hydrocarbon gas used as a propellant in specified food applications.
expanded_summary: Isobutane is a branched form of butane, a hydrocarbon gas. It is used as a propellant, valued for its gas and pressure properties rather than as a conventional solid or liquid ingredient.
source_preparation_copy: Separated or manufactured from hydrocarbon processing streams and purified to food-grade specifications.
fact_1_copy: Used as a propellant in specified food applications.
fact_2_copy: Used for its gas/pressure properties rather than as a conventional solid or liquid ingredient.

tile_summary: Octafluorocyclobutane is a manufactured gas whose molecules contain only carbon and fluorine.
expanded_summary: Octafluorocyclobutane is a manufactured gas whose molecules contain only carbon and fluorine. Its name describes a ring of four carbon atoms (cyclobutane) with eight fluorine atoms attached.
source_preparation_copy: Manufactured by controlled fluorochemical synthesis and purified.
fact_1_copy: Used as a specialised propellant or packaging gas in limited applications.
fact_2_copy: Used for its gas/pressure properties rather than as a conventional solid or liquid ingredient.

tile_summary: Aspartame-acesulphame salt is a crystalline compound containing the two sweeteners aspartame and acesulphame in a fixed salt-like combination.
expanded_summary: Aspartame-acesulphame salt is a crystalline compound containing the two sweeteners aspartame and acesulphame in a fixed salt-like combination.
source_preparation_copy: Made by combining purified aspartame and acesulphame components under controlled conditions and crystallising the resulting compound.
fact_1_copy: Two established high-intensity sweetener components in one ingredient.
fact_2_copy: Provides a blended sweetness profile without adding the two sweeteners separately.
fact_3_copy: The ingredient contains aspartame-derived material as well as acesulphame.
